description:
## Problem
Fetcher.perform_http_request rescues `Exception` (the broadest possible type) on line ~290:
```crystal
rescue ex : Exception
  @http_client_factory.release_client(uri, client, success: false)
  raise ex
```

While it re-raises (good), the `rescue Exception` in fetch_single already catches everything. This creates confusing control flow where some exceptions are caught twice.

Also, `fetch_single` rescues 6 different exception types individually. While thorough, the pattern is verbose and each rescue block does nearly the same thing (log + return failure). Some of these could be consolidated.

## Proposal
1. In perform_http_request: remove the broad `rescue ex : Exception` — the ensure block pattern or a more targeted rescue is safer
2. In fetch_single: group related exceptions that share the same handling:
   - Network errors (Socket::Error, IO::Error, IO::TimeoutError) → one rescue
   - Security errors (OpenSSL::SSL::Error) → one rescue  
   - URI errors (URI::Error) → one rescue
3. Consider using an ensure-based cleanup pattern instead of re-raise in perform_http_request

## Benefits
- Clearer exception flow
- Less risk of accidentally swallowing important exceptions
- Easier to add new exception handling without missing a rescue
title: Consolidate broad exception rescue in perform_http_request
